origin has distinct_count 3 (the three NYC airports) and time_hour has distinct_count 4341 near-unique UTC hourly instants; together origin plus time_hour plausibly identify one hourly observation per station.
wind_gust has null_rate 0.745505 (null_count 9702 of 13014), so it is retained as nullable rather than dropped, per the never-drop-for-nulls rule.
year, month, day, and hour land as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sample_value and distinct_value for each is integral (e.g. month 1.0-6.0, hour 0.0-23.0), justifying a cast to INTEGER.
time_hour lands as VARCHAR but all sample_values are ISO-8601 with a Z suffix, and the operator context confirms it represents a UTC instant, justifying a cast to TIMESTAMP.
wind_dir sample_values are integral degree multiples of 10 supporting an INTEGER cast, but null_rate 0.016828 (null_count 219) means nulls are retained rather than imputed.

purpose: This table holds cleaned hourly weather observations from the three NYC airports (EWR, JFK, LGA) for January through June 2013, sourced from ASOS via the Iowa Environmental Mesonet as packaged in nycflights13, intended to join against flight records on origin and time for weather-impact analysis.
usage: Join on origin and time_hour (UTC) to flight-level tables; consumers should expect wind_gust to be null for the large majority of rows (null_rate 0.745505) and should explicitly handle nulls in wind_dir, wind_speed, and pressure rather than assuming zero or filling them.
limitations: The cleanup only drops Airbyte capture metadata and casts types; it does not impute or filter any null values, so wind_gust remains sparsely populated (74.6% null), pressure is 11.5% null, and wind_dir is 1.7% null, and consumers must handle these nulls themselves. No duplicate rows were found (duplicate_row_rate 0.0) so no dedupe logic was applied.
